Only two code paths in the patient chart call the framework's `useAbortController`, both in workspace forms. Each passes the hook's controller into save and fetch functions, so a change to the hook's behaviour (when it aborts, when it creates a new controller, or when it aborts on unmount) would reach those saves and fetches.

**Call sites in the patient chart**

- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/lab-results/exported-lab-results-form.workspace.tsx` calls the hook at line 70. The controller is used at lines 254 (`fetchSavedLabResults`), 304 and 338 (the lab result save and fulfiller-update calls).
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx` calls the hook at line 87. The controller is used at lines 231 and 267 when saving vitals and biometrics.

**Downstream functions that receive the controller**

- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/lab-results/lab-results.resource.ts` (lines 265–333) passes the signal into `fetchSavedLabResults` and `updateOrderFulfillerDetails`.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts` (lines 533–550) passes the signal into the vitals save request.

**The hook itself and its mocks**

- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useAbortController.ts` (lines 25–38) defines the hook. It creates a new controller when the current one is missing or already aborted, and aborts it on unmount.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/mock.tsx` (line 108) and `mock-jest.tsx` (line 103) mock the hook for tests. They would only be affected if their mock behaviour were meant to track the real hook.

Other patient-chart code calls `new AbortController()` directly rather than the hook, so a change to the hook would not reach it. I did not check whether those direct uses are otherwise related to the hook.
